headline: THE RETRIEVAL BLOCKER IS CLEARED, AND IT NEVER NEEDED THE REBUILD. The recorded remedy was to rebuild llama-cli with -DLLAMA_BUILD_UI=OFF, filed as an operator step with no approved wrapper. The same pinned build advertises --jinja and --chat-template-file, and a pass-through Jinja template renders the messages verbatim -- so the -st turn feeds the model exactly the prompt as written. Stock binary, unmodified, which is the constraint that actually mattered.
evidence: Released base weights, same GGUF (sha256 1d45ce41...), same binary: copy control 0.0 templated -> 1.0 pass-through; passkey d256 1.0; mqar d256 1.0. runs/eval/diag-passthrough/ against runs/eval/diag-llamacpp-template/. The 150M proxies were never asked to retrieve -- they can.
how_it_was_found: scripts/retrieval_eval.py --probe. The scoring guards raise on a build that cannot measure a base model, which is right for a run and useless for 'then what DOES this build support?', and there is no approved way to run llama-cli --help. So the blocker was written as an environment fact from a traceback. --probe reports the flag families, the pass-through route, and the sibling binaries as data. Reach for it first on any llama.cpp question. It also confirmed there is no llama-completion and no llama-server here, which was the other half of the guess.

fix_2: retrieval_scored_from answered on the artifact digest alone, so the invalid templated stage-A cards counted as already-scored: the chain would skip them, the gate would keep refusing them, and the column would stay unmeasured with nothing left that would run. DECODE IS NOT, while the retrieval lane is still running: decode_bench is a timing measurement and a CPU pass beside it makes the absolutes a report about the box. Run `export` and `retrieval` now, and `decode` after the retrieval lane finishes -- not `all`, which would run decode into the contention. Stage-B retrieval will now measure rather than record zeros.

Stage C takes at most two finalists and is gated on deadline reserve AND prior discrimination; if stage B does not separate the arms beyond the parameter margin, the preregistered answer is to record that and not spend 1B tokens.

cost_note: The retrieval evaluator loads the model fresh for every item -- 408 items per arm at per_depth 50 -- so an arm is ~2.3h of CPU, and the whole 4-arm pass ~9h. That is the honest cost of the measurement, not a defect to work around, but it is why stage-B retrieval should start before phase 7 rather than after.
